bullets.title: Q3 GDP +3.4%, Core PCE 0.32% MoM — Economy Hot, Fed to Hike Dec & March
bullets.body: Q3 real GDP printed 3.4% q/q saar (nominal +5.9% y/y), driven by consumer spending +3.8% and capex +12.7%; private domestic demand hit strongest pace since 2021Q2 at 4.9%. Core PCE came in at 0.32% MoM with supercore services at 3.4% 6-mo annualized, and 52% of PCE categories running above 3% y/y. Consensus view: Fed hikes 25bp in December (77-84% probability per prediction markets and futures) with a follow-on March hike increasingly likely; savings rate hit 4-year low of 3.75% as consumers draw down buffers.

bullets.title: AI Hardware Imports Halve GDP Contribution — Net Capex Signal Closer to 0.5pp
bullets.body: Multiple macro commentators flag that AI hardware is almost entirely imported, creating a systematic trade drag that subtracted 3.3pp from Q3 GDP. Net exports deficit was extreme in Q3, meaning the widely cited 'core GDP' (real final sales to private domestic purchasers) overstates underlying strength. The true net AI contribution to growth is estimated closer to 0.5pp vs. sell-side estimates of 1pp+.

bullets.title: ECB on Clear Hiking Path — December Hike Very Likely, March Risk Skewed Higher
bullets.body: JPMorgan notes ECB left rates unchanged but Lagarde stated the Council 'could have' hiked at this meeting; direction of travel toward further hikes is clear to all GC members. Underlying inflation remains stable above target, tightening financial conditions via higher long rates and sovereign spreads are insufficient to deter, and no QT discussion occurred. December hike seen as near-certain; risk skewed to additional moves into 2027.

bullets.title: Prediction Markets: Dem Midterm Sweep at 66%; Fed at 4.25% Year-End; AI Bubble Burst 23%
bullets.body: Prediction markets assign 91% probability to Democrats winning the House and 67% for Senate (66% sweep), with no recession through 2026 (6% probability). Fed benchmark rate seen at 4.25% by year-end (77%), WTI oil at $80+ by year-end (83%) and $100+ at 44%. AI bubble burst by June 2027 assigned 23% probability; Anthropic IPO at 92% likelihood this year with $2T valuation at 73%.

bullets.title: Dem Sweep Adds 0.1–0.4pp to 2027 Consumption via SNAP/Medicaid Rollback
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates SNAP and Medicaid cuts represent a 20bp headwind to 2027 consumption forecasts. A targeted delay under a Democratic majority adds ~0.1pp upside; full reversal including work requirements adds ~0.4pp, most meaningful for low-income consumers. Midterm-related SNAP/Medicaid changes are seen as the dominant deficit swing factor versus defense spending differences.

bullets.title: GOOGL -11.5% as Search Miss Reignites AI Monetization Concern; GCP +103%
bullets.body: Google Search grew only +12% vs. buyside expectations of +14-15%, with AI Mode queries driving lower monetization per query. GCP grew +103% but investors assign a lower multiple due to TPU sales (lower margin). Options volume on GOOGL hit 238% above 30-day average; Citi cut PT to $375 from $447 while maintaining Buy with lower conviction.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure +48% Beats Hard, Guides 49-50% for Q4; $25B Bond Raise
bullets.body: Microsoft Azure accelerated to 48% y/y constant currency with Q4 guidance of 49-50%, beating consensus by ~4 points. MSFT raised $25B in bonds — first issuance in 9+ years — and expects FCF positive in FY27; operating margin held ~50% despite heavy AI infra investment. M365 Commercial grew +18%; Foundry revenue >3x y/y; agentic solution customers +5x. PT raised to $680 (Buy) at Citi.

bullets.title: ORACLE Investor Day: $225B Revenue by FY30, FCF >$30B by FY29, Only $20B More Capital Needed
bullets.body: Oracle targets 34% revenue growth in FY27 accelerating to $225B+ by FY30 (35% CAGR) with >40% operating margins and EPS >$21. The key surprise: only $20B additional capital needed through FY30 (vs. prior market assumption of ~$60B), turning FCF positive in 2H FY28 and targeting >$30B FCF in FY29 vs. prior consensus of $7.3B. $664B RPO with >90% tied to infrastructure; peak capex in FY27-28 stepping down in FY29. Stock +10.7%; 80% buy-rated, avg PT $240.

bullets.title: NOW -18–20% Post-Earnings: cRPO Deceleration and Margin Compression Disappoint
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q3 subscription revenue beat by only ~$8M (thinnest in 20 quarters); cRPO grew +20.3% y/y but Q4 guidance stepped down to +18.5% cc — the sharpest deceleration in the disclosed series, ~16.75% ex-Armis acquisitions. Non-GAAP gross margin fell 300bps y/y to 80.2% (4th consecutive sequential decline) as AI deployment costs surge; PS gross margin deteriorated to -19.5% from +11.1%. AI ACV raised to $1.7B for 2026 (+70% YTD) but debate centers on whether AI is cannibalistic to core cRPO. Multiple banks cut targets.

bullets.title: DASH Acquires CART for ~$17B; Both JPM Ratings Suspended
bullets.body: DoorDash announced acquisition of Instacart for ~$17B (~$65/share, 75% cash / 25% stock), a 26% premium to Oct 22 close, with $500M+ expected annual synergies. 3Q DASH organic GOV grew +23% y/y, orders +28%, revenue +34%, adj. EBITDA $1.06B (~3% above consensus). JPMorgan — acting as financial advisor to DASH — suspended ratings and price targets for both; Citi maintains Buy on DASH at $255 PT (~50% upside) on ~24x 2027E EV/EBITDA.

bullets.title: WFE Cycle Topping: Hedgeye Cuts 2027-28 Equipment Spending Estimates, Exits AMAT Long
bullets.body: Hedgeye exited its AMAT long after a ~40% gain, revising 2027 WFE guidance down $10B to $220B and 2028 down $10B to $265B, well below buyside expectations of $280-300B. 2028 could mark a cyclical peak with a potential air pocket in 2029. Key risks: China share losses structural, advanced packaging expectations too high, HBM/memory optimizations reducing equipment intensity per AI accelerator. Forward P/E in low-to-mid 20s seen as insufficient protection.

bullets.title: Mega-Cap Tech Positioning: Long MSFT/AAPL, Short GOOGL/META; QQQ Failing at ~725
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro show is long Microsoft, Apple, and Tesla; short Google and Meta in mega-cap. QQQ failing at key levels (~725) and needs to reclaim to reverse a lower-high setup. Russell 2000 short preferred over S&P 500 short; VIX bullish trend around 16.9. Adding to South Korea/DRAM shorts on bounces; long USD and Brent Oil (medium-term upside to ~119 from ~114); short precious metals and long PFIX (bond vol ETF).

bullets.title: Broad Pre-Market Tape: Software Selloff Cascades; CVNA +8%, LITE +7%, MRVL -11%
bullets.body: Pre-market color shows NOW -19.4% and GOOGL -11.6% dragging 13+ software/cloud names lower. MRVL -11.2% on reports of discussions to acquire Lumentum (LITE +7.4%). CVNA +8.4% after SEC closes investigation with no enforcement action. S&P 500 futures +0.34% to 7,757; 10-year yield +3bps to 5.00%; WTI +1.37% to $101.37. Neocloud stocks (CRWV, NBIS) lower after MSFT capacity constraint commentary.

bullets.title: FTNT -26%: Services Growth Miss Signals Cybersecurity Cycle More Hardware/Pricing-Led
bullets.body: Fortinet 3Q revenue +1% above consensus but services revenue missed and decelerated; delayed activations signal pull-forwards and customer hesitation. Product growth deceleration from +52% in Q2 to +37% in Q3; gross margin guidance disappointed. BofA downgraded to Neutral, cutting PT to $140 from $220. GS sees product revenue trough in 2Q26; 40+ cybersecurity names declined in sympathy as markets demand normalized growth proof.

bullets.title: MasterCard Q3 Beat Across the Board; Q4 Revenue Guided High-End Low-Double-Digits
bullets.body: MA Q3 revenue $9.81B (+1.6% vs. $9.66B consensus); EPS $5.31 vs. $5.17 est. Gross dollar volume +7%, purchase volume +9%, cross-border +11% local currency, switched transactions +9%. Q4 and FY26 net revenue growth guided at high-end of low double digits. New BVNK acquisition adds stablecoin capabilities; HDFC Bank small business deal adds 3M cards; travel wins expected to generate >$20B incremental spend over contract lives.

bullets.title: AI Funding / Capital Stack: ORCL Model Cuts Incremental Need to $20B; CRWV/NBIS Have Similar Levers
bullets.body: 22V notes ORCL's path to FCF positive in 2H FY28 slashes additional funding needs from ~$60B to ~$20B, with CRWV and NBIS having analogous levers (GPU financing, vendor compute financing, customer pre-payments, bring-your-own-compute). CRWV 2032 bonds recovered to 82.7% of par after early-October gap down; compute spot prices remain robust with contracts rolling higher. Goldman Sachs hosting dedicated AI funding call covering post-ORCL implications and credit financing conditions.

bullets.title: Sector Rotation into Defensives as Tech/AI Complex Corrects; Industrials Break Support
bullets.body: Tech/AI complex correcting with XLK underperforming; defensive rotation into XLV (+2%), XLU (+1%), XLE (+1%) while SPY -40bps. Industrials (XLI) broke support, down ~2% last week vs. healthcare +1.5%; 10-year Treasury yield down 30bps since Oct 8 with curve flattening materially and 10yr hovering at 5%. Negative correlation between yields and stocks broke in early October, flagging potential growth deceleration signal.

bullets.title: DoJ Assessing Nvidia-Hugging Face Deal; FTC Scrutinizes Personalized Pricing at Uber/DASH
bullets.body: Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face is being assessed by the US DoJ over AI competition concerns. The FTC ordered Uber and eight other companies (including Walmart and Delta) to hand over personalized pricing data. Google faces a criminal probe in Finland over suspected environmental law violations at a planned data center site.

bullets.title: FCC Modernizes Direct-to-Device Spectrum Rules, Expanding SCS Bands from 5 to 13
bullets.body: The FCC adopted a proposal to modernize D2D licensed spectrum rules, increasing Supplemental Coverage Space bands from 5 to 13 and adding 482 MHz for satellite-to-device services. The proposal seeks to eliminate burdensome geographic and lease requirements, replacing rigid criteria with adaptable license areas and coexistence agreements, and harmonizing SCS and mobile-satellite service rules.

bullets.title: APP and UNITY: Hedgeye Short APP, Long U as Vector Share Gains Accelerate
bullets.body: AppLovin missed its revenue guide midpoint in 2Q26 for the first time in 15 quarters; AXON model change cut returns for mid-core games and Net Revenue Per Install growth slowed to 58% from 93%. Unity Vector grew 23% sequentially vs. internal plan of 12-13%, passed $1B+ ARR two quarters early, and U.S. advertiser count is up 37% since early July vs. 10% for AppLovin. Primary research shows buyers reporting better returns on Unity; one shifted ~10% of spend out of APP. Both report next week (APP Nov 4, U Nov 5).
